correctness.rationale: All stationary Borel measures are classified using F B=I and the exact recurrence for F^n mu. At or below p=1/2, bounded signed-total-variation norms force F mu=mu and B mu=mu, hence the unique biased Bernoulli measure. Above p=1/2, a geometric inverse-branch series is an affine bijection with all forward-invariant seed measures. Lebesgue-seeded density is an explicit positive series of independent binary-digit products; finite L^s iff the s-moment multiplier is strictly less than one, including correct divergence at equality via lower bounds. L-infinity fails on positive-measure constant-digit cylinders at the sharp multiplier boundary. 3,066 exact cylinder algebra checks passed, but analytic proof, not tests, establishes infinite statements. No incorrect weak-topology homeomorphism for a discontinuous interval map is asserted.

value.rationale: The motivating primary article identifies general branch-selection probabilities and stationarity as an open direction. The exact L^s regularity curve identifies which biased expansions retain controlled stationary concentration, and the separate sharp L-infinity transition includes a genuinely borderline all-finite-L^s-but-unbounded density. Simultaneous stationary AC, singular-continuous and dense-atomic laws explain why one-point physical regularity cannot be inferred from existence. These are natural parameter boundaries rather than arbitrary computations; no general unproved extrapolation is made.
